newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which comes amid signs of division within the Labor Party over its position on a goods and services tax, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday added his support to calls for the Government to deal with tax reform if elected for a second tem, saying "there is unfinished business with the agenda of the 90s". Page 1.

According to Kerry Packer's chief Internet strategist, PBL Online head Daniel Petre, despite the arguments put forward by the Federal Government, News Ltd and PBL that the Internet would add to diversity, it could be 10 to 20 years before the Net adds suficient diversity to the media to allow current cross-media laws to be abandoned. Page 1.

Under a deal which will reduce the penalty rates at upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd, clearing the way for an extension of trading hours and bringing conditions into line with its major competitor, Myer-Grace Bros, David Jones is to pay about 7,000 employees nationwide an 11.33 per cent pay rise over two years. Page 3.

The Transport Workers Union Federal Council voted yesterday to black ban air travel by Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane and his deputy Stephen Grenville if they did not provide a satisfactory explanation of their position regarding the RBA's role in opposing a recent pay claim for truck drivers. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to the first post-Budget Newspoll, last week's Budget failed to arrest the slide in support for Prime Minister John Howard or boost support for his Government, with support for the Coalition at just 41 per cent, and only one third of voters considering the Budget will be good for the economy. Page 1.

According to the Asia Pacific Profiles, released yesterday as a 15-nation analysis under the sponsorship of The Financial Times and conducted by the Australian National University Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, there will be a lift in growth in the East Asian area this year, despite the dip in economic growth in 1996 and speculation that the growth "miracle" may be over. Page 1.

In a day of proceedings yesterday which was enlivened when an alleged fan burst into the New South Wales Industrial Court and threw a package at the judge, former Witness presenter Jana Wendt alleged she had been lured from Channel Nine to Channel Seven with promises that were never fulfilled. Page 1.

In a move which comes after the release of a five-year abortion study by the National Health and Medical Research Council, the Australian Democrats called on Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge last night to ease restrictions on the availability of the abortion drug RU486. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In an unprecedented move, the Federal Government has condemned the final report of the inquiry into the removal of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families before it has even been tabled in Parliament. The Coalition is tipped to reject the report's call for compensation and a national day to commemorate the removals. Page 1.

As the outbreak of the devastating fruit disease fire blight continues to shake the Australian apple and pear industry, New Zealand scientists testing plant material from Australia's botanic gardens have added Adelaide to Melbourne as a possible source of the disease. Page 1.

Two emotionally disturbed sisters, aged 11 and 13, have been living in a bush humpy made of wooden planks and bushes with four or five other adolescents deep in the bush near the Blacktown Pistol Club at Shalvey in Sydney's west for three weeks because the Department of Community Services was unable to find alternative accommodation for them. Page 1.

Two weeks after being dubbed "Black Jack" Moore after he declined an invitation to address steelworkers in Newcastle, going instead to the opening of the Crown Casino, Federal Industry Minister John Moore finally made it to the city yesterday, 20 days after BHP announced plans to close its steel-making operations in the area. Page 2.
THE AGE

In the strongest indication yet that the Federal Government may reconsider a goods and services tax, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said yesterday there was "unfinished business" on tax reform. Fischer will support the case for a GST by making a push today on one of the side benefits, lower petrol costs. Page 1.

In a move which comes as Victorian apple and pear growers face big losses because of interstate bans on their produce, Federal Primary Industries Minister John Anderson yesterday ordered a more intensive investigation into how the plant disease fire blight might have arrived in Australia. Page 1.

The Melbourne Coroner's Court was told yesterday 26-year-old Stewart Anthony Marshall, who died in February last year from mixed drug toxicity after taking methadone, anti-depressants and tranquillisers, was bound to die because he did not receive immediate paramedic help. Page A3.

A Supreme Court jury was told yesterday 28-year-old painter Alan Richardson murdered his fiancee, 24-year-old Joanne Campbell, by stabbing her at least 22 times after she threw a box of invitations at him during an argument about their planned wedding. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
